subject: Post-demo: data retention exception & PII handling next steps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@findata.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo recap + quick questions on retention

Hi Emma — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and two asks so we can scope an accurate proposal: 

1) Main ask: FinData confirmed you want no persistent storage of PII for scoring requests (effectively 0-retention for PII). Can you confirm the list of fields you consider PII for the use case? (e.g., SSN, email, account_id, full name)
2) Secondary: retention window for non-PII telemetry/logging (trace ids, latencies, aggregated errors). What is your target retention window for those logs (30/90/365 days)?

Proposed next steps: if you confirm the PII field list, we’ll draft a short retention exception clause and a proposed custom retention schedule (separate buckets for PII vs non-PII). I’ve copied Monica (solutions) to jump in on implementation details.

Attachments: demo-deck-20260224.pdf (slide deck)

Thanks — talk soon,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
--
Redwood Inference
https://redwood.ai
From: Emma Li <emma.li@findata.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@findata.com>, Legal (FinData) <legal@findata.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + quick questions on retention

Thanks, Dylan — great demo. Quick answers:

- PII fields: email, phone, full_name, national_id, account_number, ssn. Anything that can be used to re-identify a natural person should be treated as PII.
- Non-PII telemetry: prefer a 30-day window for anything that contains user-level identifiers; aggregated system metrics can be retained longer but must be anonymized.

Raj (cc’d) is our security lead — he’ll validate from a controls perspective. Legal is copied for contract redlines (they’ll likely want explicit language about 0-retention for PII and a defined process for evidence requests).

Emma Li
VP Product, FinData Analytics
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: FW: Post-demo recap + quick questions on retention — ask from FinData

FYI thread from Emma. Key constraints: 0-retention for PII fields listed; 30-day for user-level telemetry; aggregated anonymized metrics OK beyond that.

Can we get sign-off on whether we can propose a custom retention schedule (PII = 0 days, non-PII logs = 30 days) and surface any implementation caveats (e.g., how KV cache interacts with ephemeral PII)? Also need to know if we’ll accept contract language that mandates 0-retention for PII (we can provide an attestable flow plus audit logs that show deletions) or if we need legal to counter.

Monica — do we have a standard engineering implementation note to attach?

Thanks,
Dylan
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FW: Post-demo recap + quick questions on retention — ask from FinData

Dylan — we can implement the requested split. Implementation notes (summary):
- PII: mark requests at ingestion with PII flag; write-through to ephemeral cache only; do not persist to disk-backed logging; retention = 0 (immediately remove from in-memory cache after response flush). We can provide an audit event stream that records deletion events (no payload).
- Non-PII telemetry: bucketed logs with TTL; default 30d for user-level, aggregated metrics retain 365d (anonymized).
- KV cache: if customer pins to a model that uses KV caching containing PII tokens, we must either: (a) use ephemeral session-only caches that are destroyed on session end, or (b) provide a 0-retention flag that prevents caching of PII tokens.

I’ll attach a short proposal PDF and a checklist for security to review.

Attachments: retention-proposal-20260227.pdf

Monica
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@findata.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@findata.com>, Legal (FinData) <legal@findata.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 08:16:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed retention exception & implementation notes (draft)

Emma/Raj/legal — following up with a concise draft that aligns with what we discussed. High level: 

- PII: 0-retention. Any request flagged as containing PII will not be persisted to disk logs or long-term caches. We will provide deletion audit events (timestamp + request id, no PII payload).
- Non-PII telemetry: default 30-day TTL for user-level logs (request/response metadata without PII). Aggregated/anonymized metrics retained up to 365 days.
- KV cache: option A (ephemeral per-session KV) or option B (disable KV for requests tagged PII).

I’ve attached retention-proposal-20260227.pdf which includes the technical checklist and the exact contract language we suggest for the SOW / DPA. If this looks good, we can ask Legal to intake the short redline and then I’ll work with your security to schedule a 30-minute ops call to validate the audit events.

Next steps: please confirm approval or provide redline requests by EOD Mon (Mar 1).

Thanks,
Dylan
From: Emma Li <emma.li@findata.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@findata.com>, Legal (FinData) <legal@findata.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed retention exception & implementation notes (draft)

Received — thanks for the clear draft. I’ve reviewed at a high level; FinData legal will run a quick redline on the contract clause but the technical approach looks acceptable. Raj will coordinate with Monica to validate the deletion audit events.

We’re provisionally OK to proceed with the suggested schedule (PII = 0, non-PII logs = 30d) pending legal redline. Please share the Drive writeup (I don’t see the attachment in Gmail; perhaps a Drive link is easier).

Emma
VP Product, FinData Analytics
